_doc: The routed-inputs check of the cross-section-consistency skill: one read-only checker per group of routed
citations (a unit here is a group, not a section). Before running: cross_refs.py on the integrated manuscript,
with a unit map giving one unit per section and one for the opening part; then put each by-pair file of
xref/by-pair/ into exactly one group, and each candidate cycle of xref/cycles.tsv into one group.
Run with the writing-workflow driver: rollout.py routed-check.json --dry-run, then without --dry-run.
The editor merges the group reports into one mismatch table (assets/mismatch-table.template.md); after the
repairs (rollout.repair.example.json), run the targeted re-check: rollout.routed-recheck.example.json.
The groups below are examples: one per cited section (a heavily cited section split by its citing sections),
and the opening part's pointers into the proof part in a group of their own.

vars.manuscript: SET-ME: the canonical manuscript directory, compiled (main.tex, main.aux, main.pdf)
vars.xref: SET-ME: the output directory of cross_refs.py run on that manuscript
vars.report: SET-ME: the editor's merged mismatch table (used by the re-check only)
vars.lean: SET-ME: the Lean source at the pinned commit
vars.graph_db: SET-ME: the dependency database built by lean-dependency-graph
vars.graph_hint: query the dependency database with sqlite3 -readonly {{graph_db}} (table nodes: name, kind, module, path, line, used); only rows with used = 1 count

G1.title: statements of Section 15 cited by Sections 16 and 17

G2.title: statements of Section 16 cited by Section 18

G3.title: the opening part's citations of the proof sections, and the crosswalk
